experiment: Within-problem early compressibility, cued base at T 0.6: does the sample that later hits the cap have a more compressible opening than a sample of the same problem that finishes?
recipe: File s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (rln3_gen rows). Define ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')) using Python zlib at level 9. Group rows by problem_index. A problem qualifies if it has at least one row with cap_hit true and at least one row with cap_hit false and len(text) >= 3000 characters. For each qualifying problem take C = the cap_hit true row with the lowest sample value and F = the cap_hit false row with len(text) >= 3000 and the lowest sample value. Compute rC = ratio(C.text[:3000]) and rF = ratio(F.text[:3000]). Score 1 if rC < rF, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over qualifying problems. Problems with no qualifying pair are excluded. Report the number of qualifying problems too.

experiment: Does pre-loop compressibility predict a later rule-A loop in cued base answers at T 0.6 / top-p 1.0?
recipe: File iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (run_cell rows, 500 MATH-500 answers). Keep rows with len(text) >= 6000 characters that either have loop_A false or have loop_A true with onset_A_char >= 7000 (rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char missing or below 7000 are dropped). For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:6000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:6000].encode('utf-8')). Statistic: AUROC of -s as a score for loop_A == true over the kept rows (Mann-Whitney form, ties count 0.5). Cap hits are not used as the label; only loop_A is. Report the number of kept rows and positives.

experiment: Is the cued base's opening text at T 0.6 more self-similar than RL's opening text on the same problem?
recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (base, cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (RL step 2,800, plain). Use only rows with sample == 0 in each file. Pair the two files by problem_index. Keep pairs where both texts have len(text) >= 3000 characters; problems missing from either file are excluded. For each pair compute rB = ratio(base.text[:3000]) and rR = ratio(rl.text[:3000]), with ratio(s) = len(zlib.compress(s.encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(s.encode('utf-8')). Score 1 if rB < rR, 0.5 if they are equal, else 0. Statistic: mean score over kept pairs. Report the number of kept pairs.

experiment: Within each prefix kind of the RLN-4 K continuations, does compressibility of the stored text predict a cap hit?
recipe: Files s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/modal_k-01/k_a/K_own.jsonl and .../k_a/K_rl.jsonl (rln4_gen rows; prefix_kind own_prefix / rl_prefix). Use the stored text field as it is. Keep rows with len(text) >= 3000 characters, and drop rows with loop_A true and onset_A_char missing or below 4000. For each kept row compute s = len(zlib.compress(text[:3000].encode('utf-8'), 9)) / len(text[:3000].encode('utf-8')). Within each file separately, compute the AUROC of -s as a score for cap_hit == true (Mann-Whitney, ties count 0.5); if a file has no cap hits or no non-cap rows after filtering, its AUROC is undefined and the statistic is the other file's AUROC. Statistic: the unweighted mean of the two AUROCs. Report each AUROC and its row counts.

experiment: Pooled within-problem concordance of length with wrongness for the cued base: over all (right, wrong) pairs of finished attempt-0 samples of the same problem, the fraction in which the wrong sample has more new tokens.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows whose score_v3 is null/missing. Group by problem_index. Within each problem, form every pair (i, j) with score_v3_i == 1 and score_v3_j == 0. Pair value: 1 if n_new_j > n_new_i, 0.5 if n_new_j == n_new_i, 0 otherwise. Statistic = sum of pair values over all problems / total number of pairs over all problems. Problems with no such pair contribute nothing. Cap-hit rows and later attempts are not used.

experiment: The same pooled within-problem concordance for the RL model.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows whose score_v3 is null/missing. Group by problem_index. Within each problem, form every pair (i, j) with score_v3_i == 1 and score_v3_j == 0. Pair value: 1 if n_new_j > n_new_i, 0.5 if n_new_j == n_new_i, 0 otherwise. Statistic = sum of pair values over all problems / total number of pairs over all problems. Problems with no such pair contribute nothing.

experiment: Mean within-problem Spearman correlation of n_new with score_v3 for the cued base, over problems whose finished attempt-0 samples include at least one right and one wrong.
recipe: File studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0 and cap_hit == false; drop rows with null/missing score_v3. Group by problem_index; keep problems with at least one row with score_v3 == 1 and at least one with score_v3 == 0. For each kept problem compute the Spearman rank correlation between n_new and score_v3 over its kept rows (ties get average ranks; skip a problem if all its n_new are equal). Statistic = unweighted mean of the per-problem correlations.

experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base and RL plain endpoints
recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T2 (RL plain) = s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl; T3 (base plain) = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. Use all rows of each file (500 each, cap hits included, no filtering; if a problem_index occurs twice keep the first row; missing rows are simply absent). For each row, rate = 1000 * (number of matches of the case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in the field text) / max(n_new, 1). Let m = median of the T2 rates (numpy.median). F_X = fraction of rows of file X with rate >= m (ties at m count as >=). Compute F_theta, F_T2, F_T3. Statistic S = (F_theta - F_T3) / (F_T2 - F_T3). Report S to 3 decimals.

experiment: Answer-format-based share estimate in theta0.25_plain against the plain base
recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl; T3 = s3 r4/modal_t3-01/t3/T3.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included; first row per problem_index. A row is an 'answer-line' row if its text field contains no occurrence of the substring \boxed AND at least one line of the text, after stripping leading whitespace and any leading '*' or '#' characters, starts with the case-sensitive string 'Answer:'. s_X = (answer-line rows of X) / (rows of X). Statistic P = 1 - s_theta / s_T3. If s_T3 < 0.05 the statistic is undefined.

experiment: Accuracy of theta0.25_plain boxed answers against RL plain on the same problems
recipe: Files: theta0.25_plain = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-163704-ffca/answers.jsonl (field score_v3); studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (field t2_right, grader v3, keyed by problem_index). Keep theta rows whose text contains the substring \boxed (cap hits included if they contain it; first row per problem_index). Drop rows whose problem_index has no entry in per_problem.json. For each kept row d = score_v3 (as 0/1; missing or null score_v3 counts as 0) - t2_right (as 0/1). Statistic D = mean of d over kept rows.

experiment: Wait-rate-based share estimate in theta0.25_cue against the cued base and RL cue endpoints
recipe: Files: theta0.25_cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153102-b029/answers.jsonl; RL cue = iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153110-e985/answers.jsonl; T1 (base cue) = s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. All rows, cap hits included, first row per problem_index. rate = 1000 * (matches of case-sensitive regex \bWait\b in text) / max(n_new, 1). m = numpy.median of the RL-cue rates. F_X = fraction of rows of X with rate >= m. S_cue = (F_theta - F_T1) / (F_RLcue - F_T1). If F_RLcue - F_T1 < 0.1 the statistic is undefined.

experiment: Re-check rate after wrong vs right non-final candidate answers in RL's T2 texts, as a ratio
recipe: File: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (all 500 rows, cap hits included). Field text. Candidates, in text order: (a) each '\boxed{' with brace-balanced content (candidate string = content; skip if unbalanced before end of text; end = index after the matching '}'); (b) each match of the case-insensitive regex 'answer is:?\s*' followed by the span up to the first newline, '. ' or end of text (candidate string = that span with '$', '\(', '\)', '*' and a trailing '.' removed); (c) each line matching '^\s*\**Answer:?\**\s*(.+)$' (candidate = group 1, cleaned as in b). A box inside a (b)/(c) span counts once, as the box. Grade each candidate right iff the equivalence function of grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the one behind score_v3) judges it equal to the row's gold; empty strings are wrong. Keep only non-final candidates: at least 800 characters of text follow the candidate's end. Re-check flag = the case-insensitive regex '\b(wait|hmm|let me (double[- ]?)?check|let me verify|double[- ]?check)\b' matches in the 800 characters after the candidate's end. Pool candidates over rows. r_W = flagged/total among wrong candidates, r_R = same among right candidates. Statistic = r_W / r_R. Report it even if there are few wrong candidates.

experiment: Difference-in-differences of re-check rates, RL (T2) minus base (T1), wrong minus right non-final candidates
recipe: Apply the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1 to s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and to s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue), all 500 rows each, cap hits included. For each file compute r_W and r_R (pooled over rows). Statistic D = (r_W(T2) - r_W(T1)) - (r_R(T2) - r_R(T1)). If a file has zero non-final candidates in a class, that rate is 0.

experiment: Share of final-right answers containing a right non-final candidate followed by a re-check: RL minus base
recipe: Files: s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl (RL) and s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (base + cue). Recompute each row's final score with grader/rln4_grader_v3.py (the score_v3 procedure). Keep rows whose final score is right and that are not cap hits (cap_hit false). For each kept row, use the candidate extraction, grading, non-final filter and re-check flag of prediction 1. The row counts 1 if it has at least one right non-final candidate with the re-check flag set, else 0. F(file) = mean over kept rows. Statistic = F(T2) - F(T1).

experiment: MATH-500: share of RL's wrong finished samples whose answer equals one of the base's wrong finished answers on the same problem
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (base) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (RL). Keep rows with attempt == 0 only (4 samples per problem per model). A row is 'answered' iff cap_hit is false and extracted_v3 is a non-empty string after normalisation; a row is 'wrong' iff answered and score_v3 == 0. Normalise extracted_v3 by: delete all whitespace; strip leading/trailing '$'; replace '\dfrac' and '\tfrac' with '\frac'; delete '\left' and '\right'; delete one trailing '.'. Base wrong set W_b(p) = set of normalised extracted_v3 of base wrong rows on problem_index p. Denominator: all RL wrong rows (all problems). Numerator: RL wrong rows whose normalised extracted_v3 is in W_b(p) for their problem (empty W_b counts as no match). Missing problem rows count as empty sets. Report numerator/denominator.
unit: fraction of RL wrong finished samples

experiment: MATH-500: on problems where the base repeats a wrong value, share of RL's wrong finished samples that equal the base's most frequent wrong value
recipe: Same files, filters, 'answered', 'wrong' and normalisation as the first prediction (attempt == 0 only). For each problem p, count normalised extracted_v3 strings over base wrong rows; p is an 'attractor problem' iff the maximum count is >= 2. Modal set M(p) = all strings with that maximum count (ties: all tied strings are in M(p)). Denominator: RL wrong rows on attractor problems. Numerator: those whose normalised extracted_v3 is in M(p). Report numerator/denominator; if the denominator is 0, report 0.
unit: fraction of RL wrong finished samples on attractor problems

experiment: MATH-500: RL vote fix rate on base-vote-wrong problems where the base has a repeated wrong value
recipe: Attractor problems as defined in the second prediction (from rows.jsonl, attempt == 0, base wrong rows, max count of one normalised wrong string >= 2). Vote outcomes from studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/readout.json and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/readout.json, key per_problem, procedure 'vote' (0/1). Set A = problems with base vote == 0 that are attractor problems. Report the fraction of A with RL vote == 1. Problems missing from either readout are dropped.

experiment: MATH-500: RL vote fix rate on base-vote-wrong problems without a repeated base wrong value
recipe: Same files and definitions as the third prediction. Set B = problems with base vote == 0 that are NOT attractor problems (no normalised base wrong string appears in >= 2 of the base's 4 attempt-0 rows; this includes problems whose base rows are all cap hits or unanswered). Report the fraction of B with RL vote == 1. Problems missing from either readout are dropped.

experiment: hard328: when both single samples are wrong and finished, share where base and RL give the same answer
recipe: Files: s3 results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain). One row per problem_index; join on problem_index. 'Answered' and 'wrong' and normalisation exactly as in the first prediction (cap_hit false, non-empty normalised extracted_v3, score_v3 == 0). Denominator: problems where both rows are wrong. Numerator: those where the two normalised extracted_v3 strings are identical. Problems missing in either file are dropped.

experiment: Standardised paired gap (RL plain minus base cue, grader v3) on the clean harder 328, post-cutoff problems minus pre-cutoff problems, matched on RL answer length.
recipe: Files: s3 results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../abaybektursun-1114-151540-86ef/answers.jsonl (RL plain). Join on unique_id and drop any unique_id missing from either file. Source label of each unique_id: as recorded in results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (the file whose flag == 'none' items define the 328). post = AIME 2025 or HMMT Feb 2025; pre = every other source. right = score_v3 == 1 as stored; cap hits keep their stored score_v3 (normally 0). Strata: sort the joined problems by the RL row's n_generated ascending, break ties by unique_id ascending, and cut into 4 consecutive groups of equal size (the remainder goes to the last group). In each stratum s and group g, d_gs = mean over problems of (RL right - base right). Weights w_s = (number of post problems in s) / (number of post problems). Drop any stratum that has post problems but no pre problems, and renormalise w over the remaining strata. G_g = sum_s w_s * d_gs. Statistic = 100 * (G_post - G_pre), in points.

experiment: On harder-328 problems both models solve, the base's answer length relative to RL's, pre-cutoff minus post-cutoff.
recipe: Same two files, join, drops and post/pre labels as the first prediction. Keep problems where score_v3 == 1 in both rows and cap_hit is false in both rows. For each, r = ln(base n_generated / RL n_generated). Statistic = median of r over kept pre problems minus median of r over kept post problems (for an even count, the median is the mean of the two middle values). If fewer than 5 post problems are kept, the statistic is recorded as missing and the prediction counts as refuted.
unit: difference of median log length ratios

experiment: MATH-500: per-token entropy of the cued base's own short right answers relative to its long right answers.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln5/map-01/checks.json (key per_row, list T1) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. For each T1 row, per-token entropy e = sum_entropy_own / n_own. Drop rows with n_own == 0. Join with per_problem.json on problem_index. Keep problems with t1_right true and t1_cap_hit false. short = t1_generated_tokens <= 2000; long = t1_generated_tokens > 2000. Statistic = median e over short / median e over long (median as in the second prediction).

experiment: MATH-500: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base hit the cap and was wrong
recipe: Read studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; select problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == true. Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl (code_cue); join on problem_index (if an index has several rows, use the first in file order; a missing row counts as wrong). Statistic: number of selected problems with score_v3 == 1 in 0203, divided by the number of selected problems.

experiment: MATH-500: Code-RL cue fix rate minus random-difference cue fix rate on base clean-finished-wrong problems
recipe: Read studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; select problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == false (set W). Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl (code_cue) and iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl (random_cue); join each on problem_index (first row in file order per index; a missing row counts as wrong). Statistic: (count of W with score_v3 == 1 in 0203 minus count of W with score_v3 == 1 in 6429) divided by |W|.

experiment: MATH-500: cap-hit rate of Code-RL cue answers
recipe: Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl; keep the first row per problem_index (500 problems). Statistic: number of rows with cap_hit == true divided by 500 (a missing problem counts as not a cap hit but stays in the denominator).

experiment: hard328: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base hit the cap and was wrong
recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_wdiff328-01/abaybektursun-1114-181216-a619/answers.jsonl (Code-RL cue). First row per problem_index in each. Select problems where e72c has cap_hit == true and score_v3 == 0. Statistic: number of selected problems with a619 score_v3 == 1 divided by the number selected; a problem missing from a619 counts as wrong; problems missing from e72c are excluded.

experiment: hard328: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base finished without a cap hit and was wrong
recipe: Same two files and first-row rule as the previous recipe (e72c base cue, a619 Code-RL cue). Select problems where e72c has cap_hit == false and score_v3 == 0. Statistic: number of selected problems with a619 score_v3 == 1 divided by the number selected; a problem missing from a619 counts as wrong; problems missing from e72c are excluded.

experiment: hard328: cap-hit rate of Code-RL cue answers
recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_wdiff328-01/abaybektursun-1114-181216-a619/answers.jsonl; first row per problem_index. Statistic: number of rows with cap_hit == true divided by 328 (a missing problem counts as not a cap hit but stays in the denominator).

experiment: Paired cap-hit rate difference, RL step 100 minus base, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0100/P_math500.jsonl (A) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B). In each file keep only rows with sample == 0. If a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep the problem_index values present in both A and B (set S; problems missing from either file are dropped). Statistic: (number of rows in A over S with cap_hit true) / |S| minus (number of rows in B over S with cap_hit true) / |S|. cap_hit is the boolean field; a row with finish_reason == 'length' and cap_hit missing counts as a cap hit. Report the difference as a fraction.

experiment: Paired cap-hit rate difference, RL step 400 minus base, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (A) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B). In each file keep only rows with sample == 0. If a problem_index appears more than once, keep the first row in file order. Keep the problem_index values present in both (set S; missing problems dropped). Statistic: fraction of S with cap_hit true in A minus fraction of S with cap_hit true in B. A row with cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length' counts as a cap hit.

experiment: Paired cap-hit rate difference, RL step 400 minus base, plain prompt, clean harder 328 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_hard.jsonl (A), s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_hard.jsonl (B), and the clean list results/rln3/rln3_overlap.json (keep the problems whose flag == 'none'). Match rows to the clean list by unique_id. Keep rows with sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first in file order. Keep the clean problems present in both A and B (set S; missing ones dropped). Statistic: fraction of S with cap_hit true in A minus fraction of S with cap_hit true in B. cap_hit missing with finish_reason == 'length' counts as a cap hit.

experiment: Where step 400's accuracy on finished answers lies between base and step 2,800, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, grader v3.
recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/base-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B), .../r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl (M), .../r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (E). In each file keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the problem_index values present in all three files (set S). Grade every row with grader v3 (studies/rlneurons grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to text and gold); ignore the stored v1 score. For each file, finished = rows in S with cap_hit false (cap_hit missing counts as false only if finish_reason == 'stop'). acc_X = (finished rows with v3 right) / (number of finished rows); empty or unparseable answers count as wrong. Statistic: (acc_M - acc_B) / (acc_E - acc_B). If acc_E - acc_B <= 0, report the statistic as undefined.

experiment: Share of step-400 cap hits that are rule-A loops, plain MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95.
recipe: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s0400_s0100-01/out/s0400/P_math500.jsonl. Keep sample == 0 and, for duplicates, the first row in file order. Keep the rows with cap_hit true (cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length' also counts). For each such row, apply rule A to the text field. For every character position p that is 0 or follows a newline, with at least 8,000 characters from p to the end, take w = text[p:p+8000] and compute r = len(zlib.compress(w.encode('utf-8'))) / len(w.encode('utf-8')), using Python zlib at its default level. The row is a loop if any such r < 0.10. A row with fewer than 8,000 characters is not a loop. Statistic: loop rows / cap-hit rows. If there are no cap-hit rows, the statistic is undefined.

experiment: First-marker regrade of the base's wrong T1 answers: among T1 rows graded wrong by grader v3 on the full text, the fraction whose first answer marker is right.
recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (500 rows, base + cue, T 1.0). For each row, v3_last = grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to the full text against gold (recomputed, since the record has no v3 column). First marker = whichever of these starts earliest in text: (a) a line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', with content = the rest of that line; (b) the first '\boxed{', with content = the brace-balanced contents. first_score = grader v3 applied to the string 'Answer: ' + content against gold. A row with no marker gets first_score 0. Filter: rows with v3_last == 0, cap hits included. Statistic: (rows with first_score == 1) / (rows with v3_last == 0).

experiment: Direction of first/last disagreement on T1: among rows where the first-marker grade differs from the last-marker grade, the share that are first-right and last-wrong.
recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl, all 500 rows, cap hits included. v3_last and first_score are defined exactly as in the previous recipe (first marker = earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{'; no marker gives first_score 0). Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Statistic: (discordant rows with first_score == 1) / (discordant rows). If there are no discordant rows, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Net first-marker gain for the base on the four Day-1 #3 samples: (first-marker right count minus stored v3 right count) over all attempt-0 rows.
recipe: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (base + cue, T 1.0, 4 samples). Filter: attempt == 0 (500 problems x 4 samples = 2,000 rows; missing rows are dropped and the denominator is the number of rows present). v3_last = the stored score_v3. first_score as in the first recipe (earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{' content, graded by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py as 'Answer: ' + content; no marker gives 0; cap hits included). Statistic: (sum of first_score - sum of v3_last) / number of rows.

Normalisation N(s): if s is entirely \boxed{...}, take the inside; remove '$', all whitespace, '\left', '\right', '\displaystyle', '\,', '\!', '\;', '^\circ', '^{\circ}'; replace '\dfrac' and '\tfrac' with '\frac'; drop one trailing '.'; if the result contains '=' and none of '<', '>', '\le', '\ge', take the part after the last '='. A gold counts as an integer if N(gold) matches ^-?\d+$; otherwise it is non-integer. Equivalence E(a, g): false if either string is empty, or either N-string contains ',' or '\cup' (tuples, sets, intervals). Otherwise parse N(a) and N(g) with sympy.parsing.latex.parse_latex. It is false on any parse error, on unequal free-symbol sets, or on a timeout of 5 s per pair. With no free symbols, compare the evaluated values. With symbols, substitute 5 points (numpy default_rng(0), each symbol uniform on [0.5, 2.5], the same points for both). True iff every evaluation is finite and real and |a - g| <= 1e-6 * max(1, |g|). Denominator: rows with non-integer gold, score_v3 == 0, cap_hit false, and at least one of extracted_v3 or extracted non-empty. Numerator: those rows where E(extracted_v3, gold) or E(extracted, gold) is true. Report numerator / denominator. Cap-hit rows are excluded. Ties do not arise (one row per problem). Missing rows are excluded from both counts.
